minutes_text:
Arts Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 17, 2024

A meeting of the Inglewood Arts Commission was convened on April 17, 2024.
Commissioner Lesure called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Commissioner Aletha Metcalf ‐ District 1, Commissioner Olivia Alvitre -
  District 2, Commissioner Phyllis Battle ‐ District 3, Commissioner Vicki
  Perryman-Banks - District 4, Commissioner Jacques Lesure - Commissioner
  at Large

  Absent: None

City Personnel present were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Director
  Helen Lessick  Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant

GUEST SPEAKER. Allen Kwabena Frimpong, from ZEAL a creative led development is a 3-
year resident and business owner at 6755 West Boulevard and is an urban planner. He
received a grant last year from Bay Area Foundation and recently launched a survey to
see how artists are sustaining themselves after the Pandemic. Findings will be shared with
Commission in May.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Banks and seconded by Commissioner Battle
that the minutes for the Arts Commission meeting held on January 17, 2024, be approved.
The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Alvitre, Battle, Banks and Lesure.
Noes: None

  1
   Arts Commission

VERBAL REPORTS-Public Art Related Projects.
  a. Kia Forum Public Art Restoration Update: Christopher Jackson, Development
  Services Director, informed the Commission that when The Forum was sold to
  the Ballmer Group, management didn’t realize the medallions were art and
  were paved over. It has been decided that the owners will have the medallions
  recast and replaced in their original placements.
  b. Utility Box Art Restoration Update: Creative House Designs approved in
  January:
   Vinyl wrap vendor subcontracted in March
   Box preparation starts in late April, vinyl wraps installed in May
   Creative House community event is scheduled for June 29th
   Contract ends on July 30, 2024
  c. Senior Center Public Art Reinstallation Update: on March 22, 2024 Roots was
  reinstalled and the artist covered all of the costs for reinstallation.
  d. Morningside Library Remodel and Public Art Planning: The Library is currently
  being remodeled and will open later this year and we are waiting on their
  public art plan.
  e. Otis Collect Report on the Creative Economy 2024: the impact of the writers
  and actors strike was minimal. They saw a modest growth despite strike. Arts
  and culture is at $1.2 trillion dollars.

PUBLIC REMARKS. None

COMMISSIONERS’ COMMENTS/INITIATIVES/ART CALENDAR.
  a. KCRW Zocalo at Crenshaw High School-May 9, 2024
  b. Moon gallery: Inglewood Artists’ artworks on International Space Station
  c. Next Arts Commission Meeting: May 15, 2024 at 6:30 p.m.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Lesure declared the
meeting adjourned, at 7:02 p.m.
